definitionEn: a natural power of the mind or body, such as reason, speech or hearing
senseNote: Здесь — врождённая умственная или физическая способность (речь, слух, разум); значение «факультет» или «профессорско-преподавательский состав» не рассматривается.
situation: Talking about a natural mental or physical power, such as memory, reason or hearing, especially when praising or worrying about someone's health.

examples.text: After the accident, doctors were relieved that his mental [[faculties]] were completely unaffected.
Philosophers have long debated whether reason is a uniquely human [[faculty]].
Grandad is ninety-three, but his [[faculties]] are as sharp as ever, so don't try to trick him at cards.

texts: Memory is often the first [[faculty]] to fail with age.
Language may be the single most complex human [[faculty]].
A good detective relies above all on the [[faculty]] of observation.

badCollocation.noteRu: Faculty — умственная или сенсорная способность (речь, слух, память, суждение). Способность бегать марафон — просто the ability.

collocationTask.prompt: keep all your ___ well into old age
collocationTask.explanationRu: «Сохранить ясность ума до старости» — keep your faculties. Habits, customs и possessions — привычки, обычаи и имущество, а не умственные способности.

nuance.text: Reading other people's emotions is a [[faculty]] some children develop very early, almost like an instinct.
nuance.explanationRu: Faculty — врождённая способность ума или органов чувств. Skill — навык, которому специально учатся; здесь способность врождённая, «почти инстинкт».

reverse.text: She picked up the [[skill]] of speed-reading after a two-week course.
reverse.explanationRu: Навык, приобретённый на курсе за две недели, — skill. Faculty — врождённая способность, а не то, чему быстро обучаются.

fixIt.text: Philosophers often argue that reason is the [[instinct]] that truly separates humans from other animals.
fixIt.explanationRu: Instinct — врождённый безусловный порыв, не связанный с размышлением. Разум как умственная способность — faculty.

reply.context: A friend asks: "How's your dad doing since the operation?"
options: He's still weak physically, but his faculties are completely unaffected.
He's already back to his old faculty on the football pitch.
We are pleased to confirm that his faculties remain in satisfactory working order.
reply.explanationRu: Faculties — умственные и сенсорные способности. Мастерство в футболе — это skill, а не faculty. Третий вариант звучит как справка, а не ответ другу.

rewrite.original: Even in her nineties, she can still think, remember and speak just as clearly as ever.
rewrite.frame: Even in her nineties, her mental ____ are just as sharp as ever.

definitionEn: to gradually become weaker or disappear over time
senseNote: Здесь — «постепенно слабеть, угасать» (о чувствах, надежде, интересе, памяти); прямое значение «выцветать, блёкнуть» (о цвете) не рассматривается.
situation: Describing feelings, memories, hope or interest that gradually become weaker over time until they almost disappear.

examples.text: Public support for the reform has begun to [[fade]] as living costs keep rising.
Whatever anger she felt at the time has long since [[faded]], and the two of them are close friends again.
His hopes of winning a medal were [[fading]] fast after a disappointing semi-final.

texts: Interest in the campaign will [[fade]] unless organisers offer people a reason to keep watching.
Old grudges eventually [[fade]], especially once the people involved start talking again.
Without daily practice, even a strong command of a foreign language can [[fade]] within a year.

badCollocation.text: [[fade]] in the blink of an eye
badCollocation.noteRu: Fade — исчезать постепенно, а не мгновенно. Для внезапного исчезновения нужны vanish или disappear.

collocationTask.prompt: his enthusiasm began to ___ after the first setback
collocationTask.explanationRu: Энтузиазм постепенно угасает — begins to fade. Multiply, recover и solidify с enthusiasm по смыслу не сочетаются.

nuance.text: The old rivalry between the two firms has [[faded]] over the years, though it hasn't completely disappeared.
nuance.explanationRu: Fade — слабеть постепенно, необязательно исчезая полностью. Vanish — исчезнуть полностью и часто внезапно; ослабевшее, но ещё живое соперничество vanish не может.

reverse.text: The magician made the coin [[vanish]] right before our eyes.
reverse.explanationRu: Мгновенное полное исчезновение в фокусе — vanish. Fade описывает постепенное угасание, а не трюк.

fixIt.text: After the argument, their friendship slowly [[extinguished]], though they still said hello at parties.
fixIt.explanationRu: Extinguish — потушить (свечу, костёр), обычно намеренно и сразу. Дружба, которая слабеет сама собой, fades, а не extinguishes.

reply.context: A friend says: "Do you still feel angry about what happened with your old business partner?"
options: Not really — that anger faded a long time ago.
Yes, I fade every time I think about it.
Negative, all residual animosity has since faded, as per my assessment.
reply.explanationRu: Fade — постепенно угасать (о чувствах). «I fade» о человеке так не говорят. Второй ответ бессмысленный, третий звучит как отчёт, а не реплика другу.

definitionEn: treatment of people that is equal, just and reasonable, without bias
situation: Talking about equal, just treatment of people in courts, workplaces, sport or everyday decisions, without favouritism.

examples.text: Employees praised the new manager's [[fairness]] when it came to allocating overtime shifts.
The judge's reputation rests on her [[fairness]], even in the most controversial cases.
Kids are quick to complain about a lack of [[fairness]] when the rules suddenly change halfway through a game.

texts: The whole team respected her sense of [[fairness]].
Critics questioned the [[fairness]] of the referee's final decision.
Good parenting often comes down to consistency and [[fairness]].

badCollocation.noteRu: Устойчивое выражение — fair play (нужно прилагательное, а не существительное). Fairness play так не говорят.

collocationTask.explanationRu: После the referee's нужно существительное — fairness. Fair — прилагательное, fairly — наречие, unfairness означает противоположное («несправедливость»).

nuance.text: The scheme aims for [[fairness]], not simple equality: those who need more support should get more.
nuance.explanationRu: Fairness — справедливое отношение с учётом ситуации каждого, не обязательно поровну. Equality — одинаковое отношение ко всем; здесь именно его и избегают.

reverse.text: The law guarantees [[equality]] before the court, regardless of income or background.
reverse.explanationRu: Равенство всех перед законом — equality. Fairness допускает разное отношение в зависимости от ситуации, что здесь не подходит.

fixIt.text: The company was praised for its [[equality]] in dealing with customer complaints, treating each case on its own merits.
fixIt.explanationRu: Совершенно одинаковый подход ко всем — equality. Здесь речь о справедливом подходе с учётом ситуации каждого — fairness.

wordFormation.text: Union leaders campaigned for greater [[fairness]] in how bonuses were distributed.

reply.context: A colleague says: "I heard only senior staff got the holiday bonus this year, not part-timers."
options: That doesn't sound right — fairness means everyone who contributed should share in it.
That's fine, I think fairness just means senior staff always get more.
Meh, whatever, life's not fair anyway, who cares.
reply.explanationRu: Fairness — справедливое отношение с учётом вклада каждого, а не привилегии старших по должности. Третий ответ слишком грубый и безразличный для рабочего разговора.

rewrite.original: Everyone agreed that the new manager treated all staff equally and justly.
rewrite.frame: Everyone agreed that the new manager treated all staff with complete ____.

definitionEn: having extremely serious and damaging results, without necessarily causing death
senseNote: Здесь — «роковой, губительный» (об ошибке, недостатке), необязательно связанный со смертью; буквальное значение «смертельный» (о несчастном случае, болезни) не рассматривается.
situation: Describing a mistake, weakness or decision so serious that it completely ruins a plan, relationship or project.

examples.text: Ignoring customer feedback proved [[fatal]] for the startup, which closed within a year.
The negotiator made one [[fatal]] error: he let the other side see how desperate he was.
Losing his temper in front of the panel was [[fatal]] to his chances of promotion.

texts: One [[fatal]] flaw undid an otherwise brilliant business plan.
Overconfidence proved [[fatal]] for the reigning champions, who lost in the first round.
A single [[fatal]] miscalculation cost the company its biggest client.

badCollocation.noteRu: Fatal — «роковой», для по-настоящему катастрофических вещей. Мелкую проблему называют a slight или minor inconvenience, не fatal.

collocationTask.prompt: his ___ mistake was to underestimate the competition
collocationTask.explanationRu: Роковая, всё решившая ошибка — a fatal mistake. Obvious, common и honest описывают ошибку иначе — «очевидная», «распространённая», «честная», без оттенка катастрофы.

nuance.text: One [[fatal]] design flaw brought the whole bridge down.
nuance.explanationRu: Fatal — не просто серьёзный, а гибельный, приведший к катастрофе. Serious flaw мог бы и не привести к обрушению моста; здесь нужен именно fatal.

reverse.text: There was a [[serious]] delay in the project, but the team still finished on time.
reverse.explanationRu: Задержка, которую всё же преодолели, — просто serious. Fatal подразумевает провал, а не преодолённую трудность.

fixIt.text: Underestimating the new competitor turned out to be a [[fatalistic]] mistake that destroyed the company within months.
fixIt.explanationRu: Fatalistic — «фаталистический», описывает отношение человека к жизни (вера в судьбу), а не саму ошибку. Ошибка, погубившая компанию, — a fatal mistake.

wordFormation.text: Investors say the firm's marketing strategy was [[fatally]] flawed from the very start.

reply.context: A colleague asks: "Why did the merger fall through in the end?"
options: Apparently one side made a fatal miscalculation about the other's finances.
Because both sides caught a fatal cold during negotiations, I heard.
The merger's failure can be attributed to a fatal error in due diligence, as previously outlined.
reply.explanationRu: Fatal — «роковой» (о решающей ошибке), а не буквально «смертельный». Второй вариант применяет fatal к простуде дословно, третий звучит как отчёт, а не разговор с коллегой.

definitionEn: a death that results from an accident, disaster or violence
situation: Reporting deaths caused by accidents, natural disasters, crime or war, especially in news or official statistics.

examples.text: The report recorded twelve road [[fatalities]] in the region last year, mostly involving motorcycles.
Improved safety equipment has dramatically reduced [[fatalities]] on offshore oil rigs.
Rescue teams confirmed there had been no [[fatalities]] despite the building's total collapse.

texts: Emergency services said the crash caused no [[fatalities]], only minor injuries.
The disease has caused thousands of [[fatalities]] worldwide since the outbreak began.
Better lighting on the motorway has cut night-time [[fatalities]] by a third.

badCollocation.noteRu: Fatality — существительное («смертельный случай»). «Роковая ошибка» — a fatal error, с прилагательным fatal, а не fatality error.

collocationTask.explanationRu: После one нужно существительное — fatality («один смертельный случай»). Fatal — прилагательное, fatally — наречие, fatalism — вера в судьбу, совсем другое слово.

nuance.text: Officials confirmed three [[fatalities]] and several injuries after the stadium collapse.
nuance.explanationRu: Fatalities — именно погибшие. Casualties — более широкое слово, часто включает и раненых; раз injuries упомянуты отдельно, нужны именно fatalities.

reverse.text: The report listed the total number of [[casualties]], including both the injured and the dead.
reverse.explanationRu: Здесь речь и о раненых, и о погибших вместе — это casualties. Fatalities — только погибшие.

fixIt.text: The crash left two confirmed [[victims]], while several other passengers were treated for minor injuries.
fixIt.explanationRu: Victim — общее слово, «пострадавший» (необязательно погибший). Если известно, что погибли именно двое, точнее сказать fatalities.

wordFormation.text: Officials recorded the region's first traffic [[fatality]] of the year on New Year's Day.

reply.context: A friend who works in road safety says: "They finally lowered the speed limit near the school."
options: Good — that stretch has had way too many fatalities over the years.
Good, hopefully it makes the traffic less fatality now.
It is anticipated that this measure will yield a reduction in vehicular fatalities.
reply.explanationRu: Fatalities — смертельные случаи, существительное во множественном числе. «Less fatality» грамматически некорректно, третий вариант звучит как официальный отчёт, а не разговор с другом.

rewrite.original: Three people died when the ferry capsized in the storm.

definitionEn: the course of someone's life or the outcome of a situation, seen as impossible to avoid
senseNote: Акцент на идиоматичных сочетаниях уровня C1 (seal someone's fate, a twist of fate, tempt fate), а не только на простом «то, что случится».
situation: Talking about what will inevitably happen to someone or something, especially when it feels decided by a power beyond their control.

examples.text: No matter how hard he tried to change his life, he couldn't escape his [[fate]].
The [[fate]] of the merger now depends entirely on tomorrow's shareholder vote.
By a strange twist of [[fate]], the two old rivals ended up working for the same company.

texts: It seems to be the [[fate]] of every small bookshop to eventually close.
Whatever her [[fate]] turns out to be, she says she has no regrets.
The committee will decide the [[fate]] of the old cinema next week.

badCollocation.noteRu: Fate — то, что происходит с человеком помимо его воли, а не цель, которую achieve. «Осуществить мечту» — achieve your dream или goal, но не fate.

collocationTask.prompt: a cruel twist of ___ brought the two friends back together
collocationTask.explanationRu: Устойчивое выражение — a twist of fate («ирония судьбы»). Со словом twist chance, luck и coincidence не сочетаются.

nuance.text: It was [[fate]] that brought them together at the airport that day, or so she liked to believe.
nuance.explanationRu: Fate — сила, которая, как считается, заранее определяет события. Fortune — обычно везение или богатство; «fortune brought them together» звучит как случайная удача, а не предопределённость.

reverse.text: She made her [[fortune]] trading currencies in her twenties.
reverse.explanationRu: Разбогатеть — make your fortune. Fate к деньгам не относится, это про предопределённые события жизни.

fixIt.text: However hard he tried, he couldn't escape his [[future]].
fixIt.explanationRu: Future — будущее, которое обычно можно изменить. «Escape» (избежать) подразумевает нечто неотвратимое — fate, судьбу.

wordFormation.text: That [[fateful]] decision to sell the family business changed everything.

reply.context: A friend says: "I can't believe I ran into my ex on the one day I decided to visit that city."
options: Wow, that really does sound like fate.
Yeah, I guess that's just your fate for tomorrow's meeting too.
Indeed, such an occurrence may reasonably be attributed to fate.
reply.explanationRu: Fate — судьба, нечто необъяснимое и неотвратимое, как в этой странной встрече. Второй вариант бессмысленный, третий звучит слишком официально для разговора с другом.

definitionEn: a feeling of extreme physical or mental tiredness, especially after a long effort
situation: Talking about deep tiredness of the body or mind that builds up after long effort, stress or lack of sleep.

examples.text: After the third night shift in a row, [[fatigue]] finally caught up with her.
Doctors warned that chronic [[fatigue]] can be an early sign of several serious illnesses.
Aid organisations are seeing signs of donor [[fatigue]], with charity donations falling sharply this year.

texts: Years of conflict have left the population suffering from severe [[fatigue]] and despair.
The pilot's report blamed the crash on undetected [[fatigue]] after back-to-back flights.
Voters are showing clear signs of election [[fatigue]] after months of campaigning.

badCollocation.noteRu: После feel обычно нужно прилагательное — feel fatigued. Существительное fatigue сочетается с suffer from, experience или battle.

collocationTask.prompt: she's been suffering from chronic ___ for months
collocationTask.explanationRu: После chronic нужно существительное — fatigue. Fatigued — прилагательное, tiring — «утомительный», tiredly — наречие.

nuance.text: Weeks of overwork left him with a kind of [[fatigue]] that no amount of sleep seemed to cure.
nuance.explanationRu: Fatigue — глубокое истощение сил, которое не всегда снимается сном. Sleepiness — обычное желание спать; здесь сон не помогает, значит это fatigue.

reverse.text: A big lunch always leaves me with a wave of [[sleepiness]] in the early afternoon.
reverse.explanationRu: Обычное желание вздремнуть после обеда — sleepiness, а не fatigue (глубокое истощение после долгой нагрузки).

fixIt.text: By the end of the shift, the nurses were battling severe [[exhausting]].
fixIt.explanationRu: Exhausting — прилагательное («изнурительный»); после severe нужно существительное — fatigue («изнеможение»).

wordFormation.text: The [[fatigued]] climbers were airlifted off the mountain just before the storm hit.

reply.context: A colleague says: "I just can't seem to shake this tiredness, even after sleeping nine hours."
options: That might be more than tiredness — sounds like real fatigue, maybe see a doctor.
Don't worry, that's just normal fatigue, everyone feels amazing after nine hours.
One must consider that such persistent fatigue may warrant medical consultation.
reply.explanationRu: Fatigue — глубокая, стойкая усталость, которая не проходит после сна. Второй ответ противоречив, третий звучит как медицинский документ, а не разговор с коллегой.

rewrite.original: She felt extremely tired for weeks after finishing the big project.
rewrite.frame: She suffered from ____ for weeks after finishing the big project.

definitionEn: showing approval of, or support for, something
senseNote: Здесь — «одобрительный, положительный» (об отзыве, реакции, мнении); более простое значение «благоприятный» (о погоде, условиях) не рассматривается.
situation: Talking about an opinion, review, response or decision that shows approval or support for something.

examples.text: The board gave a [[favourable]] response to the proposal, so we can proceed with hiring.
Critics were largely [[favourable]] about the director's first film, praising its originality.
The bank manager seemed [[favourable]] towards our loan application after seeing the business plan.

texts: The committee's [[favourable]] verdict came as a huge relief to the whole team.
Early reviews of the restaurant have been overwhelmingly [[favourable]].
A [[favourable]] mention from a famous chef can transform a small business overnight.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Любимый» — favourite: my favourite restaurant. Favourable — «одобрительный, положительный» (об отзыве, реакции), а не «любимый».

collocationTask.prompt: the critics gave the play a ___ reception
collocationTask.explanationRu: Тёплый, одобрительный приём — a favourable reception. Favourite — «любимый», favoured — «предпочитаемый», favouring — форма глагола favour.

nuance.text: The proposal received a [[favourable]] response from most board members.
nuance.explanationRu: Favourable — одобрительный, положительный (об отзыве, реакции). Favourite — «любимый, самый предпочитаемый»; «favourite response» бессмысленно.

reverse.text: Chocolate cake is my [[favourite]] dessert, without any doubt.
reverse.explanationRu: «Любимый десерт» — favourite dessert. Favourable здесь не подходит: оно про одобрение, а не про личные предпочтения.

fixIt.text: The teacher's [[favourite]] comments about my essay really encouraged me to keep writing.
fixIt.explanationRu: Favourite — «любимый» (один из многих). Одобрительные, положительные комментарии — favourable comments.

wordFormation.text: A well-prepared presentation puts you in a much more [[favourable]] light with investors.

reply.context: A friend asks: "How did the interview panel react to your presentation?"
options: Really well, actually — their feedback was very favourable.
Great, I think I'm officially their favourable candidate now!
The panel's reaction may be characterised as broadly favourable, pending formal confirmation.
reply.explanationRu: Favourable — одобрительный отзыв о чём-то. «Favourable candidate» — ошибка, нужно favourite. Третий ответ звучит как официальное письмо, а не разговор с другом.

rewrite.original: Most people who tried the new app said good things about it.
rewrite.frame: Most people who tried the new app gave ____ comments.
